title: Separate from Job Radar
context: Job Radar ranks job postings. The Personal GTM Engine works on companies, contacts and outreach plans, which is a different object model and a different goal.
decision: The Personal GTM Engine is a standalone workflow and does not need Job Radar as an input.
tradeoffs: Cleaner portfolio and lower coupling. It needs its own discovery sources and config.
source_internal: SPEC.md

title: n8n is the control plane
context: The project has to show GTM engineering skill and keep control deterministic.
decision: n8n owns orchestration, filtering, scoring, fallback routing and output. Clay is only used for enrichment.
tradeoffs: More build work in n8n, with control, logic and fallbacks in one place.
source_internal: SPEC.md. Also in Roadmap.md (as ADR-001) and claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md (unnumbered table).

title: Google Sheets as state layer
context: v1 needs state that is free, easy to inspect and easy to review by hand.
decision: Google Sheets holds config, output, dedupe and ops telemetry.
tradeoffs: Needs Execute Once and batch writes to stay inside quota. Note: the `seen_accounts` and `seen_contacts` ledgers later moved to n8n Data Tables (the R2 refactor, cited in Sprint 6 - Guide.md). No ADR in the project records that move.
source_internal: SPEC.md. Also in claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md (unnumbered table).

title: Deterministic gates before LLM and paid calls
context: The project must cost $0 (NFR-01).
decision: Hard filters (industry, timezone, headcount and the others) run before any enrichment, LLM call, Apollo credit or Clay credit. The project review restates the order for outreach: score, caps, channel rule, validator, then Groq, then Gemini, then the template.
tradeoffs: Some companies that look interesting but have incomplete data get dropped. More code, but spend stays at a predictable $0. The alternative was LLM-first.
source_internal: SPEC.md. Also in Roadmap.md (as ADR-002), Project_Review_and_Fixes_Guide.md (unnumbered table, with an identical copy in claude/) and claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md.

title: HITL before outreach
context: Protect reputation and avoid email and platform risk. Reputation protection is a non-negotiable NFR.
decision: The workflow drafts outreach but never sends it.
tradeoffs: Mohamed reviews the outreach queue by hand, a few minutes a day.
source_internal: SPEC.md. Also in Roadmap.md (as ADR-004) and claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md.

title: Domain as account identity
context: Company names are inconsistent across sources.
decision: The normalized domain is the primary account key.
tradeoffs: Companies without a domain are rejected or marked for manual research.
source_internal: SPEC.md. Also in claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md.

title: Enrichment as a post-write update pass with a two-output Code node
context: Sprint 3 adds website enrichment without touching the proven gate and scoring core. In n8n, a branch with zero items stops the nodes after it.
decision: Enrich rows that are already in `accounts` through an update-in-place pass. The Code node has a second output that always carries the stats package to Run Stats and Append Ops. The alternative was splitting Process Accounts into separate filter and score nodes.
tradeoffs: The core stays untouched and the ledger stays append-only. Note: later docs show the Enrich Companies node was deleted and `Fetch Website` became an HTTP Request node in R2 (Sprint 6 - Guide.md, project review F8). No ADR in the project records that change.
source_internal: Sprint 3 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-013)

title: Deterministic HTML signatures before LLM or paid enrichment
context: Tech-stack and hiring signals were needed at $0.
decision: Regex signatures on the raw website HTML detect CRM, automation, analytics and CMS tools. LLM website summaries are deferred to Sprint 6, per SPEC section 28.
tradeoffs: Costs $0, is explainable and can be cached.
source_internal: Sprint 3 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-014)

title: Clay v1 is a human-bridged table loop, not API
context: On the free tier, Clay API access depends on the plan. The UI loop (tables, waterfalls, Claygent, credit economics) is also what interviews ask about.
decision: Export from Sheets to a Clay table, then export back to Sheets (SPEC section 14, v1 usage). No API push or pull.
tradeoffs: One manual step per batch and zero spend. API automation was deferred to a Sprint 4 extension once credits are verified. The project review and the explainer repeat this decision as "Manual Clay hand-off".
source_internal: Sprint 4 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-015). Also in Project_Review_and_Fixes_Guide.md and claude/Project Explainer for NotebookLM.md.

title: Clay merge is evidence-only, no final re-score yet
context: The 5-component scoring formula in SPEC section 21 needs `contact_feasibility`, which arrives in Sprint 5.
decision: The Clay merge writes evidence only: blank-fill, a tech-stack union, and a funding upgrade from `unknown`. It does not re-score the account.
tradeoffs: Re-scoring twice would break score explainability between sprints. The final re-score comes with ADR-021.
source_internal: Sprint 4 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-016)

title: Pilot-before-batch credit discipline
context: Claygent cost is non-linear and cannot be seen before a run. The free tier is a hard limit (NFR-01).
decision: No enrichment column runs on more than 2 rows until its per-row cost has been measured against the monthly free allowance.
tradeoffs: One extra manual step per batch, which is fine at v1 volumes (10 rows or fewer per run).
source_internal: Clay Operator - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-017)

title: Feasibility enters the account score as max contact_score
context: Contact feasibility is the fifth component of the SPEC section 21 formula. Explainability (FR-11) has to survive weight changes between sprints.
decision: `contact_feasibility_score` is the highest contact score for the account. Each account is re-scored once per batch, and `score_breakdown` is extended, never replaced.
tradeoffs: Scores stay explainable across sprints.
source_internal: Sprint 5 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-021)

title: Guessed is not verified
context: SPEC section 25 compliance and protecting deliverability.
decision: Emails that are pattern-based or not verified by the provider are capped at `guessed` (30 points). Only a waterfall verification flag grants `verified`.
tradeoffs: Email confidence stays low until verified emails exist. ADR-038 builds on this rule.
source_internal: Sprint 5 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-022)

title: Wrong contacts are rejected, not deleted
context: The Contact Finder attached the wrong people to companies whose names are common words.
decision: Wrong people stay in `contacts` with status `rejected`. Their `contact_results` rows are removed so the domain gets looked up again.
tradeoffs: A few dead rows in `contacts`, in exchange for a permanent guard against drafting to them again.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 4 - Contact Precision Guide.md

title: Deterministic product-term guard before and after the LLM
context: With only a homepage title and meta description to go on, the model mixed up what a company sells with what it struggles with. Drafts pitched a commission-software company commission automation, and pitched a CRM maker a CRM.
decision: Fixed rules extract product terms: words the company repeats in its own description, minus filler and the sender's own vocabulary. The terms are passed to the model as `PRODUCT_TERMS`. Any draft that uses them outside `first_line` and `trigger` is rejected.
tradeoffs: A product described only once is missed, so human review stays the last gate. Lead-gen and enrichment vendors are not caught; that belongs to account filtering (ADR-078). Expect more first-attempt rejections and LLM calls. A second LLM call to judge relevance was rejected as costly and non-deterministic.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 5 - Pitch Relevance Guide.md

title: Person discovery degrades to HITL sourcing when providers are plan-gated
context: The Apollo and Datagma people providers in Clay both failed hard on the free tier (two refunded failures logged).
decision: Machines verify, humans discover. Decision-makers are sourced by hand into a manual Clay table, then scored and deduplicated by n8n.
tradeoffs: Costs about 0 to 12 credits, but takes manual effort per company. Superseded when contact discovery moved to the Tavily search finder (ADR-066). Manual entry (`hitl_manual`) remains only as the fallback for `NO_RESULT` accounts.
source_internal: Sprint 5 People - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-025)

title: Size-aware wording
context: Drafts said "your ops team" to companies of 11 and 14 people.
decision: At 20 people or fewer, the validator rejects "ops team". Employee count is the only signal used.
tradeoffs: HN accounts default to 15 employees, so the rule applies to them even when the real team is bigger. The cost is slightly more personal wording, which is harmless.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 5 - Pitch Relevance Guide.md

title: Outreach stage inside the main spine
context: Sprint 6 adds outreach drafting to the engine.
decision: Drafting runs as a stage inside the main workflow spine. The alternative was a separate workflow.
tradeoffs: Still one `ops` row per run, the stats-item pattern is reused and there is no cross-workflow state. Each main run gets about 5 to 25 s of LLM latency.
source_internal: Sprint 6 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-033)

title: LLM router as one Code node, config-driven chain
context: Copy the quota-aware fallback from the wavess-core LLM router.
decision: One Code node routes drafts through the provider chain and records failures per provider. The chain is set in config (`outreach.llm.chain`).
tradeoffs: Provider endpoints live in code. Models and chain order live in config.
source_internal: Sprint 6 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-034)

title: Template fallback always writes a row
context: The HITL queue must never be empty without a visible reason.
decision: When every LLM provider fails, a deterministic template draft is written with `llm_provider = template`.
tradeoffs: Template rows need a harder human review, and `risk_notes` flags them. ADR-073 reaffirms this decision.
source_internal: Sprint 6 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-035)

title: autoMap allowed on single-writer outreach_queue
context: `outreach_queue` has exactly one writer, and its headers match the router output exactly.
decision: `Append Outreach Queue` uses Map Automatically.
tradeoffs: Adding columns to the tab later means switching to manual mapping.
source_internal: Sprint 6 - Guide.md (originally ADR-PGT-036)

title: Code assembles greeting, CTA and sign-off
context: One draft had no greeting and another ended with `[Your Name]`. These are structural defects, so they need a structural fix.
decision: The model writes only `first_line` and `body_rest`. Code adds the greeting, the exact CTA from config and the sign-off. The alternative was letting the model write the whole email.
tradeoffs: Every email shares the same skeleton.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Fixes - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Channel follows email verification
context: All 4 drafts went to the `email` channel even though every email was only guessed. Guessed addresses bounce and hurt sender reputation.
decision: The channel is `email` only when `email_status` is verified or valid. Otherwise it is `linkedin_manual` if a LinkedIn URL exists, and otherwise the contact is skipped. The alternative was to email whenever an address exists.
tradeoffs: Few email drafts until verified emails exist.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Fixes - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Validator plus tool whitelist before accepting any draft
context: Prompts reduce hallucination but do not stop it. Drafts named tools that were not in the data (HubSpot for a company that does not use it, invented Stripe details).
decision: A deterministic validator checks every draft: word counts, placeholders, numbers that are not in the facts, and company tools, which may only come from `tech_stack`, `clay_summary` or the chosen proof point. A failed draft falls through to the next provider. The alternative was trusting the prompt.
tradeoffs: More fallthroughs between providers. The template is the safety net.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Fixes - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Supersede, do not delete
context: Re-drafting needs an audit trail and should not require manual row surgery.
decision: Replaced drafts are set to `approval_status = superseded` instead of being deleted.
tradeoffs: The queue keeps growing, so filter on `approval_status`.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Fixes - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Router stays a Code node
context: n8n's Basic LLM Chain has no fallback model (only the AI Agent node v2.1+ does), and the router needs custom validation between providers.
decision: The router stays a Code node instead of a native LLM node with a fallback model. This corrects an earlier statement in the project.
tradeoffs: Provider URLs live in code.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Fixes - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: One repair retry before provider fallthrough
context: The validator rejected 3 of 4 drafts on trivial rules that the model could fix (`first_line_no_company`, `li_words`).
decision: A rejected answer is retried once on the same provider, with the rejection reason added to the prompt. The alternative was to fall through to the next provider immediately.
tradeoffs: Up to 2 calls per contact per provider, so tokens per minute matter. The 2.5 s pause between contacts stays.
source_internal: Sprint 6 Patch 2 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Claim guards in the validator
context: Drafts described the sender's engine as the prospect's, claimed work that was never built, and invented quantified results.
decision: The validator rejects `wrong_perspective`, `overclaims_built` and `quantified_claim`. The alternative was relying on human review alone.
tradeoffs: Regex rules are blunt and can reject a good draft, which then goes through repair or falls to the template.
source_internal: Sprint_6_Patch_3_Guide.md (identical copy as claude/Sprint 6 Patch 3 - Guide.md)

title: A separate digest workflow
context: The digest runs on a different cadence (daily versus on demand), and a Discord outage must not affect discovery or drafting.
decision: Personal GTM Digest is its own workflow. The alternative was appending the digest to the main engine.
tradeoffs: The Sheets reads are duplicated.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: digest_log Data Table keyed outreach_id:status
context: Discord is not a database. Without a ledger, every run would post every pending row again.
decision: A `digest_log` Data Table keyed on `outreach_id:status` records what has been announced. The alternative was a `digested` column in `outreach_queue`.
tradeoffs: Avoids a second writer on the queue and lets a row be announced again once approved. One more table to maintain.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: HTTP Request, not the Discord node
context: The digest needs full control of embeds, size limits and `allowed_mentions`, plus retries and an error output.
decision: Post to the Discord webhook with an HTTP Request node. The alternative was the native Discord node.
tradeoffs: The payload shape is ours to maintain.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: No emails in Discord
context: Guessed emails are low quality, and Discord is a third-party store of personal data.
decision: Digest cards show only the contact's name, title and LinkedIn URL.
tradeoffs: Open the sheet to see the email. Note: the Digest v2 `Build Digest` code (claude/Digest v2 - Full Review Card.md) prints the contact's email and email status in the Contact field when they exist. That contradicts this decision, and no ADR records the change.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Approval happens in Sheets, not Discord buttons
context: Discord buttons need a public endpoint and a bot application, which breaks the $0, no-exposure constraint.
decision: Approval status is set in the `outreach_queue` sheet. The alternative was Discord interactions.
tradeoffs: One extra click. Digest v2 confirms that approval still happens in the sheet.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Main engine stays manual
context: Apollo's free tier returns 0 results, the Clay hand-off is a human step, and self-hosted schedules only run while the host is up.
decision: The main engine has no schedule and is run by hand. The alternative was scheduling it like the digest.
tradeoffs: Someone has to click Execute. ADR-068 applies the same idea to the order of the three workflows.
source_internal: Sprint 7 - Guide.md (identical copy in claude/)

title: Apollo as a Code node with internal fetch
context: A pluggable source must not break the Merge or the telemetry when Apollo fails.
decision: Apollo is called from a Code node with `this.helpers.httpRequest` inside try/catch, the same pattern as the Job Radar connectors. The node always returns either data or a typed error marker. The alternative was an HTTP Request node with a separate error branch.
tradeoffs: The node always runs, so Merge and telemetry never break. ADR-065 keeps this pattern for all sources.
source_internal: Sprint 2 - Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-PGT-002 in Sprint 2 - Guide.md)

title: Pluggable source contract
context: Sprint 2 adds Apollo next to the seed list, and more sources are planned. This mirrors the Wavess/Oceanss connector interface.
decision: A pluggable source is a normalized account schema, a config kill-switch and per-source telemetry. A new source only needs a mapper that outputs the normalized schema.
tradeoffs: Gates, scoring, the ledger and outputs stay untouched when sources are added.
source_internal: Sprint 2 - Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-PGT-003 in Sprint 2 - Guide.md)

title: Deterministic country-to-UTC map instead of LLM geo inference
context: The timezone gate needs an offset for each Apollo company at no cost.
decision: A static country-to-UTC table maps the country to an offset.
tradeoffs: Costs nothing, is explainable and needs no cache. Countries not in the table fall through to the existing timezone gate.
source_internal: Sprint 2 - Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-PGT-004 in Sprint 2 - Guide.md)

title: Waterfall over single provider for email finding
context: Find as many emails as possible while keeping the cost per verified email low.
decision: Email finding uses a cascade: Apollo, then Hunter, then an AI guess.
tradeoffs: In practice the Apollo API is blocked on the Free plan (ADR-060) and Tavily contacts are LinkedIn-only (ADR-070). The email waterfall now survives only as an optional Clay Work Email step.
source_internal: Roadmap.md (originally numbered ADR-003 in Roadmap.md)

title: $env read in Code nodes
context: API keys and the webhook URL must stay out of workflow JSON, so Code and expression nodes read them through `$env`.
decision: Set `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`. The alternative was a credential per node.
tradeoffs: Any Code node can read every environment variable, which is acceptable for single-user self-hosting. Since n8n 2.0 the default is `true` (Run Guide), so the setting must be checked after an upgrade or a container rebuild.
source_internal: Project_Review_and_Fixes_Guide.md (unnumbered in its ADR table, identical copy in claude/)

title: Digest posts first, then logs
context: A failed Discord post must never mark rows as announced.
decision: `digest_log` keys are written only after a successful post. The alternative was logging first.
tradeoffs: A crash between the post and the log can repeat one digest. That was chosen over silently losing one.
source_internal: Project_Review_and_Fixes_Guide.md (unnumbered in its ADR table, identical copy in claude/). The order is also described in Sprint 7 - Guide.md, section 5.7.

title: Outreach queue ledger is the source of truth
context: `contacts.status` can drift away from the queue (project review finding F7).
decision: `doneSet`, built from the non-superseded rows of `outreach_queue`, decides whether a contact can be drafted. The alternative was a status flag on the contact.
tradeoffs: The status column can drift without breaking dedupe.
source_internal: Project_Review_and_Fixes_Guide.md (unnumbered in its ADR table, identical copy in claude/)

title: Remove the source-side cap, let gates and the write cap control volume
context: The HN source stopped at 15 posts before checking the ledger, so every run read the same 15 posts again.
decision: The HN cap comes from config (400) and covers 2 monthly threads. Volume is controlled by the gates and the `max_companies_per_run` write cap. The alternative was keeping 15 and rotating through the thread with a saved cursor.
tradeoffs: Stateless and easy to explain. Process Accounts re-checks rejected posts on every run, which costs CPU only. A "rejected" ledger can be added later if this gets slow.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch - Discovery Yield Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-1 in that doc)

title: Allow unknown timezone and a score floor of 60, keep spending gates at 65
context: Most HN posts state no timezone, and HN accounts cluster at scores of 58 to 64.
decision: Set `allow_unknown_timezone = true` and `min_account_score = 60`. The contact, Clay and outreach gates stay at 65. The alternative was parsing timezones harder from HN text.
tradeoffs: More low-confidence rows in `accounts`. They cost nothing unless enrichment lifts them to 65 or more.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch - Discovery Yield Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-2 in that doc)

title: No job-board APIs
context: The pipeline needs a company domain. Arbeitnow's feed has no company website, and Remotive's free feed is a small, delayed sample with strict call limits.
decision: Do not add job-board APIs (Remotive, Arbeitnow) in this patch. The alternative was adding a domain-resolution step, which needs its own refactor sprint.
tradeoffs: Discovery stays on HN and seeds, and later the YC directory (ADR-061).
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch - Discovery Yield Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-3 in that doc)

title: Apollo off until proven
context: The Apollo request parameters did not match the docs, and the free credit allowance is small. Later, Apollo answered `API_INACCESSIBLE` on the Free plan (Sprint 7 Patch 2, section 6D).
decision: Keep `sources.apollo.enabled = false` until a 1-credit pilot passes.
tradeoffs: HN and seeds carry discovery in the meantime. The fixed Apollo code stays in the workflow, switched off, for a future paid plan.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch - Discovery Yield Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-4 in that doc)

title: YC directory as the primary free source
context: HN gives no headcount or funding and only a weak GTM signal, so the automated accounts it produced were weak.
decision: Add a `YC Directory Source` node that reads the free, keyless yc-oss JSON feed, which includes real headcount, location and topic tags. Alternatives considered: job-board APIs, paid data, more HN threads.
tradeoffs: It is an unofficial community feed that can break or lag. The pool is finite (about 6,270 companies, mostly US), and every company is YC-backed, which is a bias. The node fails soft with an error marker.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-1 in that doc)

title: Do not retune scoring in the discovery patch
context: The scorer counts generic keywords, so curated sources score high across the board and the score stops ranking them well.
decision: Leave scoring as it is. Remove generic YC tags from the description text and add a keyword gate at the source for HN.
tradeoffs: `priority` will be true for most YC accounts. A scoring recalibration needs its own sprint with before and after evidence.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-2 in that doc)

title: HN keeps running behind a strong-keyword gate
context: HN is free and occasionally surfaces a real RevOps or GTM hiring signal, but most matches came from one generic keyword.
decision: Keep the HN source, but require at least one `strong_keywords` term as a whole word. The alternative was switching HN off.
tradeoffs: HN volume drops to a handful of accounts a month.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-3 in that doc)

title: Apollo labels come from the query, not Apollo's industry field
context: Apollo's industry names never match `industries_include`, so even a correct search would be rejected at the gate.
decision: `industry` and `company_type` come from the query's own labels. The raw Apollo industry is kept after a `|` for audit.
tradeoffs: `industry` is our label, not a measured fact.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-4 in that doc)

title: Sources stay as Code nodes
context: Three sources already share one marker and telemetry pattern, and changing that mid-patch adds risk without improving yield.
decision: The discovery sources stay as Code nodes. The alternative was native HTTP Request plus Loop nodes.
tradeoffs: More code to maintain. It belongs in the planned sub-workflow refactor.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-5 in that doc)

title: Contacts come from a search API with human review, not a people database
context: The Clay people finder is gated on the Free plan, Apollo People Search is blocked on Free, and Apify LinkedIn scrapers break LinkedIn's terms. The other option was a fully manual lookup.
decision: Tavily search, restricted to linkedin.com and parsed with fixed rules, writes into the same `contact_results` tab the manual path uses. A human reviews the rows.
tradeoffs: Free and recurring (1,000 credits a month, no card), 1 credit per account, and no change to the main workflow. Coverage depends on the search index, titles can be stale, and small firms often return nothing; the `NO_RESULT` marker plus a manual row is the fallback. No emails. Supersedes ADR-025. ADR-076 and ADR-077 amend it.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-6 in that doc)

title: The contact finder is a separate workflow
context: The hand-off tab (`contact_results`) already exists, and the main workflow is a tested 59-node spine.
decision: GTM Contact Finder is its own workflow. The alternative was adding its nodes to the main workflow.
tradeoffs: Zero risk to the spine, and the finder can be re-run alone. There are now two workflows to run in order. Chaining them with an Execute Workflow node belongs in the sub-workflow refactor.
source_internal: Sprint 7 Patch 2 - Automated Discovery Guide.md (identical copy in claude/, originally numbered ADR-7 in that doc)

title: Manual run order, not one chained workflow
context: A human must review the finder's `contact_results` before the engine uses them.
decision: Run the finder, the engine and the digest by hand, in that order. The alternative was an Execute Workflow node that chains them.
tradeoffs: Three clicks per cycle, and nothing happens while you are away.
source_internal: claude/Run Guide - Sheets, Clay, n8n, Discord.md (originally numbered ADR-1 in that doc)

title: Clay is optional for a run
context: The Clay Free plan covers about 20 to 30 rows a month, and discovery already produces more than that.
decision: Contacts and drafts do not wait for Clay enrichment.
tradeoffs: Drafts for accounts without a Clay summary rely on the tech stack only and read more generic. Clay rows go first to the accounts getting contacts that day.
source_internal: claude/Run Guide - Sheets, Clay, n8n, Discord.md (originally numbered ADR-2 in that doc)

title: Tavily contacts are LinkedIn-only
context: The Tavily finder returns LinkedIn profile URLs, not emails.
decision: Contacts found by the finder carry no email, so every new draft is `linkedin_manual`.
tradeoffs: An honest gap that keeps guessed emails out of the queue.
source_internal: claude/Run Guide - Sheets, Clay, n8n, Discord.md (originally numbered ADR-3 in that doc)

title: Fix pacing before adding providers
context: 8 of 12 LLM calls failed. The cause was Groq's tokens-per-minute limit, and the circuit breaker turned one 429 into an outage that lasted the whole run.
decision: First add pacing, retry-after handling, a cooldown that lets a provider come back, and lower reasoning effort. Extra model buckets are only the safety margin.
tradeoffs: Adding providers without pacing would only move the 429 around. Drafting gets slower (6 s between drafts, waits of up to 20 s within a 4-minute run budget).
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 3 - Draft Quality and LLM Fallback Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-1 in that doc)

title: Three Groq models on one key instead of a third provider
context: Mistral and Cerebras now need a card for API access, OpenRouter's free models allow only 50 requests a day, and Groq's limits are per model.
decision: The chain is groq (gpt-oss-120b), groq:qwen/qwen3.8-27b, groq:openai/gpt-oss-20b, gemini:gemini-3.5-flash-lite, then the template.
tradeoffs: Triples capacity at no cost. One provider carries 3 of the 4 buckets, so a Groq outage leaves only Gemini before the template. The Qwen model is a preview and can be withdrawn; that shows up as a logged 404.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 3 - Draft Quality and LLM Fallback Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-2 in that doc)

title: Keep the template as the last resort
context: When every LLM fails, the engine still has to produce a visible result.
decision: Keep the deterministic template at the end of the chain. The alternative was skipping the contact. This reaffirms ADR-035.
tradeoffs: Every contact gets a row, and the failure is visible in telemetry. A template row marks the contact as used, so it has to be superseded to retry. The run budget handles slow providers without using up contacts.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 3 - Draft Quality and LLM Fallback Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-3 in that doc)

title: Homepage facts are fetched inside the Code node
context: Without a Clay summary, the LLM invented details. One free GET of the homepage title and meta description gives it real facts.
decision: The homepage fetch runs inside the `Draft Outreach` Code node, which goes against the "native nodes first" rule.
tradeoffs: No new nodes or wires in the 59-node workflow. More code in one node. It belongs in the sub-workflow refactor.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 3 - Draft Quality and LLM Fallback Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-4 in that doc)

title: One contact per company
context: One run produced 3 drafts for one company and 2 for another. Several near-identical messages to a 15-person team on the same day look automated.
decision: `outreach.max_contacts_per_account = 1`: only one live draft per company at a time.
tradeoffs: Fewer drafts per run. Rejecting a draft makes the next person at that company eligible.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 3 - Draft Quality and LLM Fallback Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-5 in that doc)

title: YC directory before search for founder lookup
context: A semantic search on a company name cannot tell two companies with the same name apart. The finder picked the wrong people for five companies with common-word names, Twenty among them.
decision: Read the public YC company page first, and accept it only when the website it lists equals the account domain. Rejected: Apollo or Clay people search (they cost credits) and LLM verification of each profile (cost, non-deterministic).
tradeoffs: Only covers YC companies, and it depends on YC's page markup. The `yc_lookup` config switch turns it off, and anything unresolved falls through to Tavily.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 4 - Contact Precision Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-021 in that doc)

title: Deterministic location gate, flag instead of drop on unknown
context: Tavily name matches attached people from other companies and countries.
decision: Reject a profile on a clear country mismatch, keep it on a match, and keep it as `tavily_unverified` when neither side states a location.
tradeoffs: Dropping unknowns would cut volume hard, since many snippets carry no location. Flagging keeps volume and moves the decision to HITL review.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 4 - Contact Precision Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-022 in that doc)

title: Competitors are filtered at the account stage, not the draft stage
context: A workflow-engine company that competes with n8n scored 91 because its site mentions n8n.
decision: Reject competitor accounts by setting their status, and exclude future ones with `keywords_exclude` ("workflow engine", "n8n alternative", "zapier alternative").
tradeoffs: The keyword list is short and maintained by hand. A competitor that describes itself differently still reaches HITL review.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 7 Patch 5 - Pitch Relevance Guide.md (originally numbered ADR-025 in that doc)

title: Public repo with sanitized exports
context: The workflows are the portfolio evidence, but raw n8n exports carry the sheet ID, Data Table IDs, credential IDs, the instance ID and a personal email.
decision: Commit only exports passed through `scripts/sanitize_workflows.py`, which replaces identifiers with placeholders and refuses to write if it finds a key, bearer token or Discord webhook URL. Raw exports live in an ignored `exports/` folder.
tradeoffs: A reader must reconnect the sheet, tables and credentials after import (documented in SETUP.md). Live data (accounts, contacts, drafts) is never committed.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 8 - Portfolio Packaging Guide.md

title: Recorded walkthrough instead of a hosted demo
context: The engine runs on a laptop and touches real API keys and real people's public data. Hosting a live demo would need an always-on server and a sandboxed data set.
decision: Show the system in a short Loom recording plus README screenshots, with contact details kept out of frame.
tradeoffs: A reviewer cannot click through the live system. The repo plus SETUP.md lets anyone reproduce it at $0.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 8 - Portfolio Packaging Guide.md

title: Sending stays manual during dogfooding
context: Free LinkedIn accounts allow only a few personalized connection notes per month, and automated LinkedIn activity breaks LinkedIn's terms (SPEC non-goal).
decision: Send approved drafts by hand, record `send_status`, `sent_at` and `reply_received` in the sheet, and measure reply rate weekly.
tradeoffs: Volume stays low (about 10 to 20 touches a week). Each touch is reviewed and personal, which is the point of the engine.
source_internal: claude/Sprint 8 - Portfolio Packaging Guide.md

title: Router inlined in the main workflow
context: The n8n build in use had no sub-workflow trigger.
decision: Keep the LLM router inside the single Job Radar workflow. Extraction into a shared component is deferred to the next project.
tradeoffs: One large workflow; the router pattern is reused by copy in the Personal GTM Engine.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: LLM router as a single Code node
context: The HTTP Request node could not place a JSON response in a field, and fetch-based calls failed in the sandbox.
decision: One Code node calls providers through this.helpers.httpRequest, a direct port of the router pattern from the Wavess internship. Temperature is passed only when numeric.
tradeoffs: Logic lives in code rather than visible nodes, so it needs its own telemetry (provider and errors per item).
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Service account and environment variables for credentials
context: Google OAuth tokens in testing mode expire after 7 days.
decision: Use a Google service account for Sheets and environment variables for LLM and Discord keys.
tradeoffs: The sheet must be shared with the service account e-mail; env changes need a container restart.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Seen-URL ledger updates in parallel
context: If no job passes the gates, a serial branch would never record what was already seen.
decision: Branch the seen-URL write off the batch slice so it runs even when zero matches are written.
tradeoffs: Two writes per run instead of one.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Dynamic config in a sheet tab
context: Thresholds and keyword lists changed weekly during tuning.
decision: A key/value config tab, parsed by a Load Config node with typed coercion, defaults and a warnings list.
tradeoffs: Every behavior change is a sheet edit; a bad value falls back to its default with a warning instead of breaking the run.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Per-source filters before the merge
context: Each source has its own noise (disclaimers, region-locked roles, "for hire" posts).
decision: Apply deterministic per-source vetoes in each mapper before the merge.
tradeoffs: More mapper code, but the shared gates only see normalized, plausible items.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Empty-run sentinel
context: An empty output halts downstream n8n nodes, so telemetry and the digest would not run.
decision: The scoring node emits a sentinel item when there are no matches; a Filter node drops it before the sheet write.
tradeoffs: One extra node; telemetry is written on every run.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Visa filter moved from API query to config
context: The visa restriction for one source was applied as an API query parameter, outside the config.
decision: Fetch everything and apply the visa restriction as a config gate.
tradeoffs: Slightly more data fetched; the filter is visible in config and can be switched off.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Rate-limit guardrails for a fragile public source
context: A public JSON API behind a web application firewall returned 429s.
decision: One request per day, an identified user agent, continue-on-error, and a config kill switch.
tradeoffs: The source can disappear for a day without failing the run.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: GCP Always Free VM for deployment
context: The pipeline must run daily at $0 without the laptop on.
decision: Docker on a GCP e2-micro Always Free VM, port bound to localhost and reached through an SSH tunnel, with a $1 budget alert as an alarm.
tradeoffs: Small VM (swap required); no public UI exposure by design.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2

title: Calibration as data
context: Output quality tuning tempted code edits.
decision: All quality tuning happens in the config tab with a rev bump: one variable per change, one ops row as evidence.
tradeoffs: Slower tuning, but every change is traceable to a run.
source_internal: Job Radar SPEC v3.2
